So.. what is this?

Mad honey is real honey. The difference is where the bees forage. In certain mountain regions, mostly Nepal and parts of Turkey, wild bees collect nectar from specific rhododendron flowers during short seasonal windows. Naturally occurring grayanotoxins from that nectar carry into the honey. That's why we measure them in every batch and give one clear limit: up to 5 g a day.

Want to learn more?
More information
How much can I eat?

Never more than 5 g a day – less than one level teaspoon. For adults only. Do not exceed this amount.

Origin story of the honey

Real Mad Honey comes from remote mountain regions where bees forage during short seasonal windows.

In Nepal, it’s often wild-harvested from cliff hives — not farmed like regular honey.

That’s why it’s rare, seasonal, and impossible to mass-produce.

Want the full story?
Mad honey vs. normal honey

It's still real honey, but in certain regions bees collect nectar from specific rhododendron flowers, and grayanotoxins (GTX) from that nectar enter the honey. Regular honey doesn't contain GTX. We publish batch lab reports so you know exactly what you're getting.

Lab Reports
What does it taste like?

Darker and more intense than everyday honey: earthy, slightly bitter, with a warm finish. Colour and texture vary by batch, because we never blend.

    The Source

    WHERE IT COMES FROM

    a honey with a story that begins at 3,500 meters above sea level.

    Centuries of tradition

    Mad honey has been collected in the Himalayas for centuries. Honey hunters still reach the cliff colonies on ropes, once or twice a year.

    Fun and Enjoyment

    The honey comes from wild colonies of the Himalayan giant honey bee, which build their combs on cliff faces above 2,500 metres.

    One short season

    Rhododendrons bloom for only a few weeks in spring. That is the only window in which this honey can be collected, which is why supply is limited.

    Never blended

    We don't blend batches. Colour, taste and grayanotoxin content differ from batch to batch, so every batch gets its own lab report.

    About mad honey

    Mad honey from Nepal is wild honey, harvested by hand in the Himalayas at a minimum of 3,500 metres.

    the harvest

    Harvested by hand: Honey hunters in Nepal collect this honey from wild cliff colonies of the Himalayan giant honey bee (Apis laboriosa), working on ropes high above the valley floor. One short window: The honey can only be collected in short seasonal windows, which is why supply is limited. Never blended: We don't blend batches, so colour, taste and grayanotoxin content differ from batch to batch, and every batch gets its own lab report.

    how to use mad honey

    Never more than 5 g a day – less than one level teaspoon. For adults only. Do not exceed this amount.

    Nepal vs Turkey

    We source our mad honey from two regions, Nepal and Turkey. Our Nepal honey is dark and earthy, harvested from high-altitude Himalayan cliffs. Our Turkey honey, from the Black Sea region, is lighter in colour with a milder flavour. Both are wild-harvested and lab-tested per batch. Not sure which to pick? Our Try-Out Pack lets you taste both side by side.

    Support / FAQ

    FAQ

    What is Real Mad Honey?

    Real Mad Honey is raw, wild-harvested honey from Nepal. It contains naturally occurring grayanotoxins (GTX) from rhododendron nectar, which is what makes it different from regular honey. We measure the grayanotoxin content of every batch. Never more than 5 g a day, less than one level teaspoon, for adults only.

    Why did you start Real Mad Honey?

    We started in 2020 after seeing “mad honey” everywhere online — lots of stories, almost no proof. We built Real Mad Honey to set a real standard: verified sourcing, batch lab testing, responsible guidance, and honest expectations.

    What makes Real Mad Honey “the international standard”?

    Because we built it around a simple checklist: Real origin (named harvest regions, not vague "Himalayan" claims). Batch-level lab reports for grayanotoxin content (not generic "lab tested" marketing). A rejection standard (we don't buy batches outside our specification). One clear limit: never more than 5 g a day, for adults only.

    How is mad honey made?

    Mad honey is made naturally by bees foraging on wild rhododendron flowers, whose nectar contains grayanotoxins. The bees turn that nectar into honey exactly as they would any other, and those compounds carry through into the finished jar. How much ends up in a given batch depends on the rhododendron species, the region, and the season it was harvested.

    How can you tell if mad honey is real or fake?

    Real mad honey comes with batch-level lab reports showing the measured grayanotoxin content and a named harvest region rather than a vague "Himalayan" claim. It is dark and thick, with a distinctly bitter finish. Without those signals there's no way to verify what's in the jar.

    What is the difference between mad honey and regular honey?

    Mad honey contains grayanotoxins from rhododendron nectar; regular honey does not. Otherwise it is honey like any other, mainly natural sugars and water. The grayanotoxins also give it a bitter, less sweet taste. It is far rarer, because it can only be wild-harvested in short seasonal windows.

    What is mad honey?

    Mad honey is normal honey, but made in places where bees collect nectar from certain rhododendron flowers during short seasonal windows. That nectar can contain grayanotoxins, which carry into the honey in naturally varying amounts.

    What are grayanotoxins (GTX)?

    Grayanotoxins are natural plant substances in the nectar of certain rhododendron species. Bees carry them into the honey. The amount differs by region, season and batch, which is why we measure it in every batch.

    Is grayanotoxin a “neurotoxin”?

    Grayanotoxins are biologically active plant substances, and larger amounts can cause dizziness, nausea and low blood pressure. That's why we measure every batch and give one clear limit: up to 5 g a day, less than one level teaspoon, for adults only.

    Is mad honey “toxic”

    Eaten in larger amounts, mad honey can cause dizziness, nausea, sweating and low blood pressure. Keep to the limit on the label: up to 5 g a day, less than one level teaspoon, for adults only. Not recommended for children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, for people with heart or blood pressure conditions, or if allergic to honey. Taking medication? Ask your doctor first.

    Is mad honey a drug?

    Yes. It is honey, sold as a food, with naturally occurring grayanotoxins from rhododendron nectar. Nothing is added.

    What does mad honey taste like?

    Darker and more intense than everyday honey: earthy, slightly bitter, with a warm finish at the back of the throat. Colour and texture vary by batch and season, and raw honey can crystallise over time. Both are natural.

    Why do people use Real Mad Honey?

    On its own from the spoon, or stirred into a drink that has cooled below 40 °C. Never more than 5 g a day – less than one level teaspoon.

    How much can I eat?

    Up to 5 g a day – less than one level teaspoon. For adults only.

    Why no more than 5 g a day?

    Because mad honey contains naturally occurring grayanotoxins, we give one fixed maximum for every batch: 5 g a day, less than one level teaspoon. Please don't exceed it.

    Do you have a measuring spoon?

    Yes, our bamboo honey spoon. Whichever spoon you use, keep to up to 5 g a day – less than one level teaspoon.

    Can I have more than 5 g a day?

    No. Never more than 5 g a day – less than one level teaspoon.

    What happens if I take too much?

    Eating more than the stated amount can cause dizziness or light-headedness, nausea, cold sweats and low blood pressure (weakness, feeling faint).

    What should I do if I ate more than 5 g?

    Don't eat any more, drink water and rest somewhere safe. If symptoms are severe or don't improve, call 112 or see a doctor.

    Who should NOT use mad honey?

    Not recommended for children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, for people with heart or blood pressure conditions, or if allergic to honey. For adults only. Taking medication? Ask your doctor first.

    I take medication – can I eat it?

    Ask your doctor first. Mad honey is not recommended for people with heart or blood pressure conditions.

    Why does every batch look and taste different?

    We don't blend our honey to a standard taste. It is wild-harvested from high-altitude cliffs in the Himalayas, so colour, flavour and grayanotoxin content differ by region, season and batch. The main harvest is in spring (April to May), when the rhododendrons bloom, sometimes followed by a second harvest in autumn (October to November). That's why every batch gets its own lab report.

    Can the same person have different experiences?

    Yes. Because we don't blend batches, one jar can differ in colour, taste and texture from the next.

    The Mark of Authenticity

    Mass-produced honey tastes the same in every jar because it is heated, filtered or blended. We don't do that, so natural variation between batches is normal. We test every batch for its grayanotoxin content, and the limit is the same for all of them: never more than 5 g a day.

    Where does your honey come from?

    We source through trusted partners in:

    • Nepal, via real relationships connected to Himalayan honey hunter communities
    • Turkey, where mad honey exists in traditional regions with rhododendron nectar
      We apply the same standard regardless of origin.

    Do you buy bulk honey and relabel it?

    No. We don’t source anonymous marketplace honey. Our sourcing is relationship-based, with origin and handling taken seriously.

    How do I know this is authentic mad honey?

    Look for: batch-specific lab reports, transparent origin details, a clear maximum amount with warnings, and a rejection standard (batches outside specification don't get sold).

    Do you publish lab reports?

    Yes — we publish batch-level lab reports so you can see what you’re buying.

    What exactly is tested in your lab reports?

    We test for GTX levels at the batch level. (And we use that to decide if a batch is acceptable.)

    What happens if a batch doesn’t meet your standard?

    We don’t buy it. If we don’t trust a batch, it never becomes a product.

    Why do you reject batches?

    Because GTX can vary. If results are outside our thresholds or anything looks inconsistent, we choose the conservative route: reject.

    What are red flags when buying mad honey?

    Red flags in a seller include: no batch lab reports, vague "Himalayan" origin claims, promises about effects or strength, no clear maximum amount, unrealistic harvest timelines (mad honey isn't harvested "fresh monthly" year-round) and no satisfaction guarantee.

    Can I mix it with coffee or tea?

    Yes. Let your drink cool below 40 °C before you stir the honey in. Never more than 5 g a day.

    Can I put it in hot tea / drinks?

    We recommend avoiding high heat (above 40 °C / 104 °F): it changes the character of raw honey.

    Can I cook with Real Mad Honey?

    You can cook with it for flavour, but heat changes the character of raw honey. Best: use it raw, or add it after cooking. The 5 g a day maximum also applies to honey in food and drinks.

    Does heat make it unsafe?

    No. Heat changes the honey's taste and character; the 5 g a day maximum stays the same.

    Do you ship worldwide?

    Yes, we ship to all countries in the world except to:

    • Turkey
    • South-Korea
    • North-Korea

    Can customs seize my package?

    Customs rules differ by country. While most shipments arrive normally, we can’t control customs decisions. If you’re unsure, check your local import rules for honey/food products.

    Can I travel internationally with mad honey?

    Often yes, but always check:

    • Destination import rules
    • Airline rules
      Tips:
    • Keep it in original sealed packaging
    • Consider checked luggage if flying
    • Verify customs rules before departure

    How should I store Real Mad Honey?

    Store at room temperature in a cool, dark, dry place. Avoid direct sunlight and heat.

    Should I refrigerate it?

    No — refrigeration can speed up crystallization and isn’t needed.

    Does mad honey expire?

    Honey is naturally stable, but each jar has a best-before date for optimal flavor and quality.

    Why is the color different from another jar I tried?

    Color varies naturally by:

    • Region
    • Season
    • Batch
      Nepal batches often appear darker; Turkey can be lighter. Natural variation is normal.

    Why does texture vary?

    Raw honey can vary in thickness and may crystallize over time — this is normal.

    How do I make my crystallized honey liquid again?

    If you prefer a smooth, liquid texture, you can reliquefy your honey: place the tightly sealed jar in a bowl of warm water (around 40 °C / 104 °F) and stir gently every few minutes. Make sure the honey itself doesn't get hotter than 40 °C: higher temperatures change the character of raw honey. Never use boiling water or a microwave.

    Where is my tracking link?

    You’ll receive tracking via email once the order is shipped. If you can’t find it or did not receive it within 24 business hours, please contact support with your order number.

    My tracking hasn’t updated in days — is my package lost?

    Sometimes carriers pause scans. If there’s no movement for an extended period, contact support with your order number and tracking so we can investigate.

    My order says delivered, but I don’t have it — what now?

    Don’t worry! In most cases, the package is nearby. Before contacting support, please follow these steps:

    1. Wait 24 Hours Sometimes couriers mark a package as "Delivered" when it has reached the local sorting hub or while it is still on the delivery truck. It often arrives the following business day.

    2. Perform a "Hidden Spot" Check Couriers often try to protect your package from theft or weather by placing it out of sight. Please check:

    • Behind large plants or pillars.
    • Under the porch or inside the garage.
    • The back door or side entrance.
    • Inside your mailbox or a shared parcel locker.

    3. Ask Your Neighbors It’s very common for a courier to accidentally deliver a package to a direct neighbor or for a household member to have brought the package inside without mentioning it.

    4. Check for a "Pickup Notice" Check your tracking link or your physical mailbox for a notice. If the courier felt it wasn't safe to leave the package, they may have dropped it off at a local pickup point or post office for you to collect.

    5. Contact the Carrier Directly If you still cannot find it, contact the shipping carrier (e.g., DHL, FedEx, UPS) immediately. They can check the delivery scan to see exactly where the driver was when they marked it as delivered.

    Still no luck? If you have completed the steps above and the carrier cannot help, please email support@realmadhoney.com with your order number. We will open a formal investigation with the courier to locate your package.

    Can I return my order?

    • How to proceed: Please contact our team at support@realmadhoney.com with your order number. We will review your request and guide you through the correct return process.

    My jar arrived damaged — what should I do?

    We take great care in packaging our honey to ensure it reaches you safely. However, if your order arrives damaged or leaking, please contact us immediately so we can make it right.

    To help us resolve the issue quickly, please email support@realmadhoney.com with:

    Once we receive this information, our team will investigate the issue and help you with the next steps, such as a free replacement or a full refund.

    Can I cancel or change my order?

    If you need to make changes or cancel your order, please contact support@realmadhoney.com immediately with your order number. We will do our absolute best to accommodate your request, but please keep the following in mind:

    The "Packed & Processed" Rule Once an order has been packed or processed by our fulfillment center, we are no longer able to cancel it or make any changes (such as adjusting the shipping address or product quantity).

    Why can’t I cancel if my tracking says "not yet shipped"? Even if your tracking link hasn't updated yet, your order is likely already deep in our logistics chain. We work with automated fulfillment centers designed for maximum speed. Once an order is "picked and packed," it is placed inside a secured shipping container or on a pallet with thousands of other orders.

    At this stage, it is physically impossible to retrieve a single box without stopping the entire shipment. Tracking numbers often only "activate" once the courier scans the entire pallet at their sorting hub, which can happen hours after your package was actually sealed.

    What should I do if it’s too late to cancel? If your order is already processed, the easiest and most cost-effective solution is to refuse the package at the door when the courier attempts delivery. By refusing the delivery, the package is returned to us free of charge. Once it arrives back at our facility, we will process your refund to your original payment method.
